report.summary: The namespace was freshly deployed at 00:28:55Z, so all telemetry starts around then and there is no pre-incident baseline. The one failing flow is the frontend's call to the recommendation service. Frontend client spans to oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations fail with gRPC status 14 and the exact message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.23.80:8080 (2026-11-24T00:32:47.393Z)'; 10.96.23.80 is the ClusterIP of Service recommendation (port 8080). The failures surface as HTTP 500 on frontend GET /api/recommendations, HTTP 504 after ~15 s on frontend-proxy GET, and HTTP 504 on the load-generator's user_get_recommendations. Prometheus reports ServiceEndpointDown firing for recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 since 00:30:49Z and HighRequestErrorRate firing at 1.00 failure ratio for GET /api/recommendations?productIds=*, which matches a total outage of that endpoint. The recommendation workload itself is not down: its pod recommendation-5dc78dffcf-m66ds is Running, its container reports ready, restartCount is 0, it logged 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080' at 00:30:21Z, and it sits at 0.0046 CPU cores and ~41.8 MB of a 500Mi limit. What is wrong is the Service: recommendation is the only application Service in astronomy-shop with spec.internalTrafficPolicy=Local (all others are Cluster), and its single endpoint is pod 10.244.234.147 on node sregym-worker, while the only caller, frontend-6765c5b7c8-d5mwn, runs on sregym-worker2. With internalTrafficPolicy=Local kube-proxy only forwards to endpoints on the client's own node, so there is no usable endpoint on the frontend's node and traffic to 10.96.23.80:8080 is dropped (timeout) rather than refused. Recommendation server spans stopped being produced (get_product_list/ListRecommendations/ListProducts rate ~0.089/s at 00:31:00-00:31:30, 0 at 00:32:00). Other services and all pods looked healthy in the sampled data, and a flagd fault was ruled out because every flag in demo.flagd.json has defaultVariant off. A secondary HighRequestLatency alert on accounting ('order-consumed' p95 5000 ms) has no baseline and no tie to this cause and is reported as an unresolved signal, not as impact.

The active frontend pod is frontend-6765c5b7c8-d5mwn on node sregym-worker2 with pod IP 10.244.7.222, and the previous frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-nlg9q was on node sregym-worker3; no frontend pod runs on sregym-worker, the only node holding a recommendation endpoint.

Frontend client spans to oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations carry otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and the detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.23.80:8080 (2026-11-24T00:32:47.393Z)'; the sampled error traces start between 00:31:10Z and 00:32:03Z.

The same requests appear as HTTP 500 on frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations', as HTTP 504 after ~15.0 s on frontend-proxy GET, and as HTTP 504 after ~15.0 s on load-generator GET spans inside user_get_recommendations.

The alerting rules loaded at query time report ServiceEndpointDown firing for instance recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 in namespace astronomy-shop since 2026-11-24T00:30:49Z with description 'Service endpoint recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 in astronomy-shop is unreachable.', and HighRequestErrorRate firing for GET /api/recommendations?productIds=* at a failure ratio of 1.00 since 00:31:26Z-00:32:26Z.

Pod recommendation-5dc78dffcf-m66ds is Running with all conditions True (Ready since 00:30:19Z), restartCount 0, started 00:30:18Z, and its container logged 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080' at 00:30:21Z.
The recommendation container consumed 0.0046 CPU cores and 41,799,680 bytes of working set against a 500Mi memory limit, so it was neither CPU-starved nor memory-pressured.

The recommendation Deployment defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe for its container; only a memory limit of 500Mi is set, so the pod's Ready condition reflects only that the container is running.

Recommendation server spans stopped: get_product_list, oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts ran at ~0.089 spans/s at 00:31:00Z and 00:31:30Z and at 0 at 00:32:00Z, and the per-service recommendation span rate had fallen to 0 by 00:32:20Z.

Average span durations over 00:27:07Z-00:32:07Z were small for the other dependencies (product-catalog 1.0 ms, cart 1.1 ms, currency 1.1 ms, payment 0.8 ms, shipping 1.9 ms, ad 1.8 ms, checkout 6.2 ms, recommendation 3.0 ms) while frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' averaged 8229 ms and load-generator user_get_recommendations averaged 10414 ms.
All 27 pods in astronomy-shop were in phase Running with every container ready and restartCount 0 at query time, including recommendation-5dc78dffcf-m66ds.
No NetworkPolicy object existed in namespace astronomy-shop at query time (the query returned zero objects), so an L3/L4 policy deny is not the mechanism for the timeouts.

Pod or node failure on sregym-worker was considered and rejected: the recommendation container was running and had logged its listener start, and other pods on the same node (cart, product-reviews, quote, flagd, kafka, llm, accounting) kept serving with 1-6 ms average span durations.

A flagd feature-flag fault injection was considered and rejected: the demo.flagd.json in ConfigMap flagd-config has every flag (including recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, kafkaQueueProblems) with defaultVariant 'off'.

The working hypothesis for how the Service came to be broken is the 00:30:18Z 'OpenAPI-Generator' update of Service recommendation that left internalTrafficPolicy=Local; the deployment-side companions at nearly the same time (recommendation ReplicaSet revision 2 at 00:29:40Z adding nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker and revision 3 at 00:30:18Z with kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, plus frontend revision 2 at 00:30:13Z pinning frontend to sregym-worker2) are consistent with the same fault-injection event pinning a single-endpoint service to Local traffic, but the exact field the update changed cannot be verified.

The concurrently firing HighRequestLatency alert for accounting (p95 5000 ms, span 'order-consumed', activeAt 00:31:26Z) is probably a separate, non-causal signal: accounting processed orders continuously (order log lines roughly every 5-15 s up to 00:31:52Z), its consumer group 'accounting' held a total lag of 1 message on topic orders, and no accounting log line reports an error after 00:29:21Z.

Reset Service recommendation's spec.internalTrafficPolicy to Cluster (or otherwise guarantee a recommendation endpoint on every node that hosts a caller), then confirm that frontend GET /api/recommendations returns 200, that oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations spans stop carrying rpc.grpc.status_code=14, and that ServiceEndpointDown for recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 clears.

Add a readiness probe to the recommendation container so that an unreachable service is distinguishable from a running pod, and give single-replica services more than one eligible node when local-only traffic policy is used.

gaps: The exact field changed by the 'OpenAPI-Generator' Update of Service recommendation at 2026-11-24T00:30:18Z is not recorded: managedFieldsSummary gives only the last write time, so whether internalTrafficPolicy=Local was written then (or came from the helm install at 00:28:55Z and only became harmful when the recommendation pod was pinned to sregym-worker and the frontend to sregym-worker2) cannot be verified.

No Service-kind Kubernetes Event was available; the events read covered 2026-11-23T23:34:37Z to 2026-11-24T00:30:19Z and contained no Service events, so the 00:30:18Z Service update is not corroborated by an event.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no audit trail exists for who or what modified the recommendation Service.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR samples in this environment (every frontend series observed was STATUS_CODE_UNSET), so the span-metric error rate could not be used; the HighRequestErrorRate alert relies on that same metric and its firing was read from the loaded rule set, not from the series themselves.

Jaeger keeps only the most recent traces, so the earliest retained recommendation failure span starts at 00:31:10Z; the actual first failing request time is unknown, and successful recommendation spans still appear at 00:31:00-00:31:30Z.

Error-tag trace searches (error=true, window 00:28:00Z-00:32:07Z) returned no matching traces for cart, checkout, payment, product-catalog, ad, product-reviews, currency, email, shipping, accounting, fraud-detection and quote; that shows only that this sampled Jaeger view had no such error spans, not that those services never errored.

The accounting HighRequestLatency signal (p95 5000 ms on 'order-consumed') has no comparable baseline because all telemetry starts around 00:28:55Z; whether it deviates from normal and what drives it remains unknown and is not tied to the recommendation outage by the evidence.

The frontend pod logs in the window did not yield readable error lines for the recommendation failures (the filtered read returned no lines), so the frontend-side view of the outage rests on its spans and the Prometheus alert, not on its application log.
next_steps: Inspect Service recommendation's history/audit outside this run (e.g. the management tooling identity 'OpenAPI-Generator') to confirm what the 00:30:18Z update changed.
After correcting internalTrafficPolicy, verify unauthenticated reachability of recommendation.astronomy-shop:8080 from a pod on sregym-worker2 as well as the blackbox probe's node.
Re-evaluate accounting's 'order-consumed' latency against a longer baseline to decide whether its HighRequestLatency alert is a real second problem or an artifact of a freshly started environment.
